ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: It has often been noted that men of genius have bad memories, and that persons having extraordinary memories, like Cardinal Mezzofanti, have little else. The truth is that there are two quite distinct kinds of memory: the memory for external facts and words, apart from their significance; and the memory for spiritual facts and principles. The man of genius, who may have no special reason for cultivating the lower kind of memory, may even find it rather a hindrance than a help. His prayer is, "Let not my heart forget the things my eyes have seen." So long as his heart retains the significance of the facts he has seen and the words he has heard, he is willing to let the words and the facts go, as a man casts away the shells after he has eaten the oysters. The "well-informed" person commonly differs from the man of genius in this: that he carries about with him all the shells of all the oysters he has ever eaten, and that his soul has grown thin under the burden.

questions.passage: It has often been ①<u>noting</u> that men of genius have bad memories, and that persons having extraordinary memories, like Cardinal Mezzofanti, have little else. The truth is that there are two quite ②<u>distinct</u> kinds of memory: the memory for external facts and words, apart from their significance; and the memory for spiritual facts and principles. The man of genius, who may have no special reason for ③<u>cultivating</u> the lower kind of memory, may even find it rather a hindrance than a help. His prayer is, "Let not my heart forget the things my eyes have seen." So long as his heart retains the significance of the facts he has seen and the words he has heard, he is ④<u>willing</u> to let the words and the facts go, as a man casts away the shells after he has eaten the oysters. The "well-informed" person commonly differs from the man of genius in this: that he carries about with him all the shells of all the oysters he has ever eaten, and that his soul has grown thin under the burden.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① noting → noted: 'It has often been noted that ~'에서 수동태(has been + p.p.)이므로 noted가 와야 한다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
❌ ① noting → noted: 'It has often been noting'이면 현재완료 수동태 구조(has been + p.p.)에 맞지 않음. noted(과거분사)가 올바름 ← 정답
✅ ② distinct: 'two quite distinct kinds of memory'에서 명사 kinds를 수식하는 형용사로 올바름
✅ ③ cultivating: 'no special reason for cultivating'에서 전치사 for 뒤 동명사로 올바름
✅ ④ willing: 'he is willing to let'에서 be willing to 구문으로 올바름
det.tip: 현재완료 수동태는 'have/has been + 과거분사(p.p.)' 형태입니다. noting(현재분사)은 수동태에 쓸 수 없습니다.

det.korean: ③ differ → differs: 'The "well-informed" person commonly differ from ~'에서 주어가 3인칭 단수(The person)이므로 differs가 와야 한다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① having: 'persons having extraordinary memories'에서 현재분사가 persons를 수식하므로 올바름
✅ ② heard: 'the words he has heard'에서 현재완료(has + p.p.)로 올바름
❌ ③ differ → differs: 'The "well-informed" person commonly differ from'에서 단수 주어 The person에 동사 원형 differ는 맞지 않음. 3인칭 단수 differs가 올바름 ← 정답
✅ ④ eaten: 'the oysters he has ever eaten'에서 현재완료(has + p.p.)로 올바름
det.tip: 주어가 'The person'(3인칭 단수)이면 동사에 -s를 붙여야 합니다. differ → differs.

det.korean: ④ which → who: 'The man of genius, which may have no special reason ~'에서 선행사가 사람(The man)이므로 who가 와야 한다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① retains: 'his heart retains the significance'에서 3인칭 단수 주어 heart에 -s 붙은 동사로 올바름

✅ ③ grown: 'his soul has grown thin'에서 현재완료(has + p.p.)로 올바름
❌ ④ which → who: 'The man of genius, which may have no special reason'에서 선행사가 The man(사람)이므로 관계대명사 who가 와야 함. which는 사물에 사용 ← 정답
det.tip: 관계대명사에서 선행사가 사람이면 who, 사물이면 which를 사용합니다. 'The man of genius'는 사람이므로 who가 올바릅니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② thick → thin: '그의 영혼이 짐 아래서 얇아졌다(grown thin)'는 부담으로 쇠약해졌다는 뜻. thick(두꺼운)은 문맥과 반대. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① extraordinary: '비범한 기억력(extraordinary memories)'으로 문맥에 적절
❌ ② thick → thin: 'his soul has grown thick under the burden'이면 짐 아래서 영혼이 두꺼워졌다는 뜻이 되어, 짐에 짓눌려 쇠약해졌다는 원문 논지와 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ③ significance: '사실의 의미/중요성(the significance of the facts)'으로 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ hindrance: '장애물(a hindrance than a help)'로 도움이 아닌 방해라는 대비 맥락에 적절
det.tip: grown thin under the burden은 '짐 아래서 수척해졌다'는 비유입니다. thick(두꺼운)은 이 비유와 반대됩니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ higher → lower: 천재는 '하위(lower)' 기억력을 기를 이유가 없다고 서술함. higher(상위)는 정반대. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① retains: '그의 마음이 의미를 간직한다(retains the significance)'로 문맥에 적절
✅ ② casts away: '굴 껍데기를 버린다(casts away the shells)'로 비유에 적절
❌ ③ higher → lower: 'no special reason for cultivating the higher kind of memory'가 되면 천재가 상위 기억력을 기를 이유가 없다는 뜻이 되어, 외부 사실의 기억(lower kind)을 기를 이유가 없다는 원문과 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ burden: '짐(under the burden)'으로 모든 껍데기를 지고 다니는 무게감에 적절
det.tip: 'the lower kind of memory'는 '외부 사실과 단어의 기억'을 가리킵니다. 천재는 이 하위 기억력을 기를 이유가 없다는 것이 원문의 논지입니다.

det.korean: 천재의 마음이 간직하는 것은 ____________이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① the significance of the facts(사실의 의미): 원문 'his heart retains the significance of the facts'와 일치 ← 정답

❌ ④ the things my eyes have seen(내 눈이 본 것들): 기도문(prayer) 속의 표현이며 retains의 목적어가 아님
det.tip: 천재에게 중요한 것은 사실 자체가 아니라 '사실의 의미(the significance of the facts)'입니다.

det.korean: 천재는 마음이 의미를 간직하는 한 기꺼이 ____________을 놓아준다.
det.analysis:

questions.passage: It has often been noted that men of genius have bad memories, and that persons having extraordinary memories, like Cardinal Mezzofanti, have little else. The truth is that there are two quite distinct kinds of memory: the memory for external facts and words, apart from their significance; and the memory for spiritual facts and principles. The man of genius, who may have no special reason for cultivating the lower kind of memory, may even find it rather a hindrance than a help. His prayer is, "Let not my heart forget the things my eyes have seen." The "well-informed" person commonly differs from the man of genius in this: that he carries about with him all the shells of all the oysters he has ever eaten, and that his soul has grown thin under the burden.
